headline: This 2019 law lets states use certain federal grant funds to pay up to 90% of costs for building or expanding public target ranges, and keeps those funds available for five fiscal years.
what_it_does: Under current law, states can use specified federal grant funds to cover 75% of the costs of building or expanding public target ranges. This law raises that share to up to 90%. It also extends the period that these funds stay available from two fiscal years to five.

who_it_affects.group: State governments that receive specified federal grant funds for public target ranges
who_it_affects.how: They may cover a larger share of construction and expansion costs, up to 90% instead of 75%, and have more time to use the money.

who_it_affects.group: Public target range operators and the local communities that build or expand public shooting ranges
who_it_affects.how: Projects that receive these federal grant funds may be partly paid for by a larger federal share, which could affect how much a state or locality must contribute.

when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on May 10, 2019. The official summary does not list a separate effective date, so the provisions appear to apply from enactment.
